name: gitea-issue-tracker
description: andesim tickets are Gitea issues at gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim; use the `tea` CLI (login "andes") with --repo nick/hybrid_sim and --description, not --body.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

"Ticket" for the andesim repo means a **Gitea issue** on the origin remote
`https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim`. There is no in-repo ticket
directory and no `.gitea/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`; the tracker was empty until
2026-09-06.

Use the **`tea` CLI** (`~/.local/bin/tea`, v0.15.1, installed 2026-09-06).
The login is already configured under the name `andes` (created from the
`~/.git-credentials` password; tea minted its own access token on the server).

```sh
tea issues create --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim \
  --title "..." --description "$BODY"
tea issues list --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim
```

Two gotchas, both cost a retry:

- The body flag is **`--description` / `-d`**, NOT `--body`.
- **`--repo nick/hybrid_sim` is required.** Auto-detection from the local git
  remote fails ("remote repository required") because the origin URL carries
  userinfo: `https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git`.

The repo has **no labels and no milestones defined**, so don't pass
`--labels`/`--milestone` until some are created. Bodies render GitHub-flavored
markdown (tables work).

Roadmap item IDs (`U10h`, `U11`, `FR-109`, ...) from the `ROADMAP_*.md` files
are the natural ticket titles — see [[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]].
---REMOTE---
origin	https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git (fetch)
origin	https://nick@gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git (push)

# #19 release: ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is the only supported engine, and S/U        
  privilege must be validated on it (open)                                    
                                                                              
  @nick created 2026-09-08 10:07                                              
                                                                              
  ## Problem                                                                  
                                                                              
  AndeSim v0.1.0 delivers exactly one cycle-accurate engine: ax46mpv_fpga_l3  
  (VLEN 1024, DLEN 1024, ELEN 64, 2 MB L3, built with three privilege levels).
  Every other engine is deferred to a later release and will not be present in
  a v0.1.0 install.                                                           
                                                                              
  Two things assume a different engine, ax45mpv_premium, which will not be    
  there:                                                                      
                                                                              
  • the environment check (andesim doctor) treats the absence of the          
  ax45mpv_premium engine binary as a **hard failure**, so the very first      
  command a new user is told to run reports an error on a correct install     
  • the end-to-end test runner picks ax45mpv_premium as its default engine, so
  the suite cannot run at all on a v0.1.0 install                             
                                                                              
  Separately, the two S/U-privilege handoff fixtures — the supervisor-mode one
  and the user-mode one — are pinned to yet another engine, ax66_makatau,     
  paired with the QEMU CPU model andes-ax66. ax66_makatau is not part of      
  v0.1.0 either, so privilege support would ship unverified.                  
                                                                              
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is also built with three privilege levels, and QEMU offers a
  matching andes-ax46mpv CPU model, so the privilege behaviour can and must be
  validated there instead.                                                    
                                                                              
  ## Required Behavior                                                        
                                                                              
  • **The environment check must report success on an install whose only      
  cycle-accurate engine is **ax46mpv_fpga_l3**.** It must not fail, and must  
  not warn, about the absence of any other engine.                            
  • **The end-to-end test suite must run against **ax46mpv_fpga_l3** when no  
  engine is named.**                                                          
  • **The S/U-privilege handoff must be exercised against **ax46mpv_fpga_l3** 
  paired with the QEMU CPU model **andes-ax46mpv**, and must pass.** Both the 
  supervisor-mode fixture and the user-mode fixture must pass on that pairing.
  If a privilege transport defect is uncovered by moving to this engine,      
  fixing it is part of this work — shipping the fixtures disabled or marked as
  expected failures does not satisfy this ticket.                             
  • Naming an engine explicitly must continue to work. This ticket changes    
  what the default and the environment check expect; it does not require      
  removing the ability to run another engine that happens to be installed.    
                                                                              
  ## Acceptance Scenarios                                                     
                                                                              
    Feature: ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is the supported engine for v0.1.0               
                                                                              
    Scenario: Environment check passes on a single-engine install             
      Given an install whose only cycle-accurate engine is "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"  
      When I run the environment check                                        
      Then it reports success                                                 
      And it does not report a failure or a warning about any absent engine   
                                                                              
    Scenario: The test suite defaults to the supported engine                 
      Given an install whose only cycle-accurate engine is "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"  
      When I run the end-to-end test suite without naming an engine           
      Then the suite runs against "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"                           
      And the suite passes                                                    
                                                                              
    Scenario Outline: Privilege handoff is validated on the supported engine  
      Given the cycle-accurate engine "ax46mpv_fpga_l3"                       
      And the functional engine configured with QEMU CPU model "andes-ax46mpv"
      When I run the <fixture> privilege handoff fixture in hybrid mode       
      Then the run completes successfully                                     
      And the fixture reports the expected result                             
                                                                              
    Examples:                                                                 
      | fixture          |                                                    
      | supervisor-mode  |                                                    
      | user-mode        |                                                    
                                                                              
  ## Compatibility and Constraints                                            
                                                                              
  • The engine pairing for privilege runs is fixed: the cycle-accurate engine 
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3 with the functional engine running the QEMU CPU model andes-
  ax46mpv. Both halves are required; a privilege handoff needs an S/U-capable 
  core on both legs.                                                          
  • Everything already supported must continue to work on this engine: the    
  fast, cycle, and hybrid modes; the marker and PC triggers; the profile      
  command; the bare-metal runtime; the Linux runtime; and state verification. 
                                                                              
  ## QA Procedure                                                             
                                                                              
  1. Prepare an install whose only cycle-accurate engine binary is            
  ax46mpv_fpga_l3. Remove or hide every other engine binary.                  
  2. Run the environment check. Confirm it reports success and says nothing   
  about missing engines.                                                      
  3. List the available engines. Confirm ax46mpv_fpga_l3 is offered and is the
  one selected when none is named.                                            
  4. Run the end-to-end test suite with no engine named. Confirm it runs      
  against ax46mpv_fpga_l3 and passes.                                         
  5. Run the supervisor-mode privilege handoff fixture in hybrid mode, with   
  the functional leg using QEMU CPU model andes-ax46mpv. Confirm it completes 
  and reports the expected result.                                            
  6. Repeat step 5 with the user-mode privilege fixture.

   3 #   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
   4 #   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
   5 #                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
   6 #                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
   7 #                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
   8 #                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
   9 #   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
  10 #                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
  11 #                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
  12 #                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
  13 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG ARGS [QEMU_ARGS...] - spawn QEMU for a plugin-only
  14 #                               drain test (boots $VSIM_ELF with the plugin
  15 #                               attached); sets RC to QEMU's exit code.
  16 
  17 TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
  18 TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
  19 
  20 if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  21   . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
  22 fi
  23 
  24 hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  25   # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  26   # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  27   # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  28   VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  29   VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  30   VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  31   VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  32   for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
  33     if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
  34       echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
  35       exit 77
  36     fi
  37   done
  38 }
  39 
  40 # Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
  41 # $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
  42 # absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
  43 hybrid_describe_int() {
  44   "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
  45     | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
  46 }

  48 # Spawn QEMU for a plugin-only drain test: boot $VSIM_ELF on andes_ae350 with
  49 # the hybrid plugin attached, stdin detached, combined output to LOG.
  50 #   plugin_qemu_drain LOG PLUGIN_ARGS [EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS...]
  51 # PLUGIN_ARGS is the plugin argument string after "$VSIM_PLUGIN," (e.g.
  52 # "outfile=$STATE"). Sets RC to QEMU's exit code -- deliberately not local,
  53 # callers gate on it -- and toggles errexit off around the spawn exactly like
  54 # every call site used to. No shared-memory backend: plugin-only tests have
  55 # no vsim leg, so nothing else ever opens the mmap, and the machine's default
  56 # RAM is the same 128 MiB the backend used to force.
  57 plugin_qemu_drain() {
  58   local log="$1" plugin_args="$2"; shift 2
  59   set +e
  60   "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  61     -machine andes_ae350 \
  62     -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  63     -nographic \
  64     -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  65     -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  66     "$@" \
  67     -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$plugin_args" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1
  68   RC=$?
  69   set -e
  70 }

  72 # Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
  73 # the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
  74 put_word_le() {
  75   local v=$3 bytes="" i

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release surface: v0.1.0 ships exactly the cycle-accurate engines named by
# shipped_cycle_engines() (lib/log.sh), because the vsim side builds only
# those. Two ways that promise rots:
#
#   1. a test pins an engine that is not shipped -- it then hard-fails (or
#      silently skips, which is worse) on a correct v0.1.0 install. This is
#      exactly what happened to the S/U privilege fixtures, pinned to
#      ax66_makatau.
#   2. a shipped engine is missing from the build dir -- the suite cannot run.
#
# Both are checked statically here, so a wrong engine reference is caught in a
# 1-second contract test instead of a 5-minute e2e timeout.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. No harness script may NAME a deferred engine in code. Full-line comments
#    are stripped first: prose that explains why an engine is deferred (and
#    which one) is documentation, not a dependency.
pat=$(deferred_cycle_engines | tr ' ' '\n' | grep . | paste -sd'|')
hits=""
while IFS= read -r f; do
  h=$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$f" | grep -nE "(${pat})" | sed "s|^|${f#$ROOT/}: |")
  [ -n "$h" ] && hits+="$h"$'\n'
done < <(find "$ROOT/tests" "$ROOT/scripts" -name '*.sh' -type f | sort)
if [ -n "${hits%$'\n'}" ]; then
  fail "harness scripts pin engines v0.1.0 does not ship:"$'\n'"${hits%$'\n'}"
fi
ok "no harness script pins a deferred engine"

# 2. Every shipped engine is present and self-describes as cycle-accurate.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
[ -n "$BINDIR" ] || fail "VSIM_BIN_DIR unset and absent from config.env"
for eng in $(shipped_cycle_engines); do
  SIM="$BINDIR/sim_$eng"
  [ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "shipped engine missing: $SIM (source ./setup.sh)"
  "$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"kind": *"cycle-accurate"' \
    || fail "$eng --describe does not report kind cycle-accurate"
  ok "shipped engine present: sim_$eng"
done

echo "PASS[andes_sim_engine_set]"
